newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakura Bank says to buy back dlr convertible bonds.
newsitem.headline: Sakura Bank says to buy back dlr convertible bonds.

text.p: Sakura Bank Ltd, one of Japan's top commercial banks, said on Friday that it plans to buy back its 2.625 percent dollar-denominated convertible bonds due March 31, 2003.

Sakura said in a statement that the offer will start on June 30 and expire on July 18. The bank said it will pay cash for the convertible bonds at a price equivalent to 92 percent of the bonds' face value plus interest.
The buyback plan is aimed at trimming outstanding debt and strengthening Sakura's financial base, while trying to avoid a potential increase in the number of its shares, it said.
As of June 25, there was $104.76 million worth of the convertible bonds outstanding. The conversion price of the bond is 2,332.60 yen, it said.
